title: M-QAM MIMO Maximum-Likelihood Detection with QAOA: ML-Rate Offline Angle Design and Correlated Infinite-Size Spin-Glass Models
abstract: The quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA) targets NP-hard maximum-likelihood (ML) detection in multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems. Existing $M$-ary quadrature amplitude modulation (M-QAM) detectors design angles by expected Ising energy: online per instance, warm-started, or ramped, while train-once designs remain B/QPSK-only or block-local, leaving M-QAM without a size-scalable benchmark. Their infinite-size spin-glass theory assumes independent disorder, matching the retained covariances at B/QPSK but not M-QAM's correlated couplings and fields. We develop a correlated infinite-size multi-species spin-glass framework whose covariance-matched evaluators make that energy an offline objective with a size-scalable benchmark. In addition, the ML rate, the exponential rate of sampling the ML string, is for the first time exploited for QAOA angle design in MIMO detection. The energy evaluator is $q$-free at $O(p\,4^p)$ cost while the ML rate transfers angles from a fixed $q_{\rm ref}$-qubit reference. Tests reach 4096-QAM, 128 antennas, $p=30$ and per-symbol SNR 0-45 dB. In simulations, ML rates fall as a power law $r_0\,p^{-α}$, with larger exponents for the sampling design, which tracks exact ML at $5\times5$ 16-QAM (0-20 dB) and $3\times3$ 64-QAM (8-28 dB) while its bit-error rate (BER) advantage widens with SNR to two orders of magnitude. The approach points toward near-optimum decoding on deeper noiseless fault-tolerant quantum (FTQ) circuits.
summary: This work tackles the difficult ML detection problem in high-dimensional M-QAM MIMO systems by formulating it as an Ising spin-glass model. The authors introduce a novel, size-scalable approach by using the ML rate—the exponential rate of the optimal solution—as the objective function to design QAOA parameters. This method shows superior performance compared to traditional energy-based quantum approaches.
main_problem: The paper addresses the NP-hard problem of Maximum-Likelihood (ML) detection in M-QAM Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) systems.
main_result: The authors develop a correlated infinite-size multi-species spin-glass framework and show that using the ML rate for QAOA angle design yields significant performance gains over energy-based designs.
method: The methodology involves mapping the detection problem to an Ising cost function, developing a correlated spin-glass surrogate, and utilizing the ML rate as a novel, size-scalable objective for QAOA angle optimization.
model_or_system: The system is an M-QAM MIMO channel, modeled by a cost function derived from minimizing the squared Euclidean distance between received and transmitted signals. This is mapped onto an Ising Hamiltonian structure, which is analyzed using correlated infinite-size spin-glass theory.
key_observables: ML Rate (exponential rate of sampling the ML string), Binary Error Rate (BER), and the energy density $\langle ar{C}_qangle/q$.
important_parameters: M-QAM constellation size (up to 4096-QAM), number of antennas (up to 128), and Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) up to 45 dB.
main_assumptions: The framework develops a correlated spin-glass surrogate, which is not mathematically proven to equal the true physical energy density limit, and the analysis relies on specific scaling assumptions for the infinite-size limit.
figures_summary: Figures compare performance metrics like SER across various detection methods (exact ML, offline design, WS pipelines) for different QAM constellations, demonstrating the advantage of the sampling-designed angles.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the ML detection problem and its mapping to an Ising model. It then develops the correlated infinite-size spin-glass framework, proposing the ML rate as a novel angle design objective. Finally, it presents simulation results showing the superior performance of the ML-rate-guided QAOA approach.
why_interesting: The connection between quantum optimization algorithms (QAOA) and complex physical detection problems (MIMO) via spin-glass theory is highly relevant. The use of the ML rate as a design parameter bridges quantum information theory with advanced signal processing.
